requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports blocking and non-blocking procedure-based communication.
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS supporting blocking procedure-based communication.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- TTCN-3 supports blocking and non-blocking procedure-based communication.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports blocking and non-blocking procedure-based communication.
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS supporting non-blocking procedure-based communication.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- TTCN-3 supports blocking and non-blocking procedure-based communication.

requirements.original: Blocking procedure-based communication is blocking on the calling and the called side, whereas non-blocking procedure-based communication is only blocking on the called side.
requirements.canonical: Blocking procedure-based communication IS blocking on the calling side and on the called side.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- Blocking procedure-based communication is blocking on the calling and the called side, whereas non-blocking procedure-based communication is only blocking on the called side.

requirements.original: Blocking procedure-based communication is blocking on the calling and the called side, whereas non-blocking procedure-based communication is only blocking on the called side.
requirements.canonical: Non-blocking procedure-based communication IS blocking only on the called side.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- Blocking procedure-based communication is blocking on the calling and the called side, whereas non-blocking procedure-based communication is only blocking on the called side.

requirements.original: Signatures of procedures that are used for non-blocking procedure-based communication shall be specified according to the rules in clause 13.
requirements.canonical: A signature of a procedure used for non-blocking procedure-based communication SHALL be specified according to the rules in clause 13.
requirements.condition: the procedure is used for non-blocking procedure-based communication
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- Signatures of procedures that are used for non-blocking procedure-based communication shall be specified according to the rules in clause 13.

requirements.original: The CALLER calls a remote procedure in the CALLEE by using the call operation.
requirements.canonical: In blocking procedure-based communication, the caller IS calling a remote procedure in the callee by using the `call` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- The CALLER calls a remote procedure in the CALLEE by using the call operation.

requirements.original: The CALLEE accepts the call by means of a getcall operation and reacts by either using a reply operation to answer the call or by raising (raise operation) an exception.
requirements.canonical: In blocking procedure-based communication, the callee IS accepting the call by means of a `getcall` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- The CALLEE accepts the call by means of a getcall operation and reacts by either using a reply operation to answer the call or by raising (raise operation) an exception.

requirements.original: The CALLEE accepts the call by means of a getcall operation and reacts by either using a reply operation to answer the call or by raising (raise operation) an exception.
requirements.canonical: In blocking procedure-based communication, the callee IS reacting to an accepted call either with a `reply` operation answering the call or with a `raise` operation raising an exception.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- The CALLEE accepts the call by means of a getcall operation and reacts by either using a reply operation to answer the call or by raising (raise operation) an exception.

requirements.original: The CALLER handles the reply or exception by using getreply or catch operations.
requirements.canonical: In blocking procedure-based communication, the caller IS handling the reply or exception by using `getreply` or `catch` operations.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- The CALLER handles the reply or exception by using getreply or catch operations.

requirements.original: The CALLER calls a remote procedure in the CALLEE by using the call operation and continues its execution, i.e. does not wait for a reply or exception.
requirements.canonical: In non-blocking procedure-based communication, the caller IS continuing its execution after the `call` operation without waiting for a reply or exception.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- The CALLER calls a remote procedure in the CALLEE by using the call operation and continues its execution, i.e. does not wait for a reply or exception.

requirements.original: The CALLEE accepts the call by means of a getcall operation and executes the requested procedure.
requirements.canonical: In non-blocking procedure-based communication, the callee IS accepting the call by means of a `getcall` operation and executing the requested procedure.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- The CALLEE accepts the call by means of a getcall operation and executes the requested procedure.

requirements.original: If the execution is not successful, the CALLEE may raise an exception to inform the CALLER.
requirements.canonical: In non-blocking procedure-based communication, if the execution of the requested procedure is not successful, the callee MAY raise an exception to inform the caller.
requirements.condition: the execution of the requested procedure is not successful
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- If the execution is not successful, the CALLEE may raise an exception to inform the CALLER.

requirements.original: The CALLER may handle the exception by using a catch operation in an alt statement.
requirements.canonical: In non-blocking procedure-based communication, the caller MAY handle an exception by using a `catch` operation in an `alt` statement.

readings: In non-blocking procedure-based communication, the caller MAY handle an exception by using a `catch` operation in an `alt` statement (and also elsewhere, e.g. as stand-alone statement).
In non-blocking procedure-based communication, a `catch` operation handling an exception of a non-blocking call SHALL be used within an `alt` statement.
ambiguity.issue: 'may' can mean that handling the exception is optional, or restrict where the catch is placed; chosen reading: handling is optional and an alt statement is one possible place.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.2 -- The CALLER may handle the exception by using a catch operation in an alt statement.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports unicast, multicast and broadcast communication:
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS supporting unicast, multicast and broadcast communication.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.3 -- TTCN-3 supports unicast, multicast and broadcast communication:

requirements.original: Unicast communication means one sender to one receiver.
requirements.canonical: Unicast communication IS communication from one sender to one receiver.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.3 -- Unicast communication means one sender to one receiver.

requirements.original: Multicast communication is from one sender to a list of receivers.
requirements.canonical: Multicast communication IS communication from one sender to a list of receivers.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.3 -- Multicast communication is from one sender to a list of receivers.

requirements.original: Broadcast communication is from one sender to all receivers (being connected or mapped to the sender).
requirements.canonical: Broadcast communication IS communication from one sender to all receivers connected or mapped to the sender.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.3 -- Broadcast communication is from one sender to all receivers (being connected or mapped to the sender).

requirements.original: This means, it is only possible to address one, several or all test components that are connected to the specified port.
requirements.canonical: A unicast, multicast or broadcast communication operation CANNOT address a test component that is not connected to the specified port.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.3 -- This means, it is only possible to address one, several or all test components that are connected to the specified port.

requirements.original: Unicast, multicast and broadcast can also be used for mapped ports.
requirements.canonical: Unicast, multicast and broadcast communication MAY be used for mapped ports.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.3 -- Unicast, multicast and broadcast can also be used for mapped ports.

requirements.original: In this case, one, several or all entities within the SUT can be reached via the specified mapped port.
requirements.canonical: When unicast, multicast or broadcast communication is used via a mapped port, one, several or all entities within the SUT CAN be reached via the specified mapped port.
requirements.condition: the communication is used for a mapped port

ambiguity.issue: 'entities within the SUT' is not defined; the addressable entities are presumably those identified by the address type at the test system interface.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.3 -- In this case, one, several or all entities within the SUT can be reached via the specified mapped port.

requirements.original: specifies the port at which the specified operation shall take place;
requirements.canonical: The send part of a sending operation SHALL specify the port at which the operation takes place.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- specifies the port at which the specified operation shall take place;

requirements.original: defines the message or procedure call to be transmitted;
requirements.canonical: The send part of a sending operation SHALL define the message or procedure call to be transmitted.

ambiguity.issue: The send part of a reply or raise operation transmits a reply or an exception, not a message or procedure call; the list is incomplete.

improper_terms.proper: message, procedure call, reply or exception

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- defines the message or procedure call to be transmitted;

requirements.original: gives an (optional) address part that uniquely identifies one or more communication partners to which a message, call, reply or exception shall be sent.
requirements.canonical: The send part of a sending operation MAY contain an address part that uniquely identifies one or more communication partners to which the message, call, reply or exception is sent.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- gives an (optional) address part that uniquely identifies one or more communication partners to which a message, call, reply or exception shall be sent.

requirements.original: The port name, operation name and value shall be present in all sending operations.
requirements.canonical: A sending operation SHALL contain the port name, the operation name and the value to be sent.

ambiguity.issue: "value" is used where a template instance (e.g. a signature template for call) is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- The port name, operation name and value shall be present in all sending operations.

requirements.original: The address part (denoted by the to keyword) is optional and need only be specified in cases of one-to-many connections where:
requirements.canonical: The address part (denoted by the `to` keyword) of a sending operation MAY be omitted.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- The address part (denoted by the to keyword) is optional and need only be specified in cases of one-to-many connections where:

requirements.original: The address part (denoted by the to keyword) is optional and need only be specified in cases of one-to-many connections where:
requirements.canonical: The address part of a sending operation NEED NOT be specified except in one-to-many connections where unicast, multicast or broadcast communication requires the receiving entities to be identified.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- The address part (denoted by the to keyword) is optional and need only be specified in cases of one-to-many connections where:

requirements.original: unicast communication is used and one receiving entity shall be explicitly identified;
requirements.canonical: In a one-to-many connection with unicast communication, the address part of a sending operation SHALL explicitly identify the one receiving entity.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- unicast communication is used and one receiving entity shall be explicitly identified;

requirements.original: multicast communication is used and a set of receiving entities has to be explicitly identified;
requirements.canonical: In a one-to-many connection with multicast communication, the address part of a sending operation SHALL explicitly identify the set of receiving entities.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- multicast communication is used and a set of receiving entities has to be explicitly identified;

requirements.original: broadcast communication is used and all entities connected to the specified port have to be addressed.
requirements.canonical: In a one-to-many connection with broadcast communication, the address part of a sending operation SHALL address all entities connected to the specified port.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- broadcast communication is used and all entities connected to the specified port have to be addressed.

requirements.original: The response and exception handling part of the call operation is optional and is required for cases where the called procedure returns a value or has out or inout parameters whose values are needed within the calling component and for cases where the called procedure may raise exceptions which need to be handled by the calling component.
requirements.canonical: The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY be omitted.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- The response and exception handling part of the call operation is optional and is required for cases where the called procedure returns a value or has out or inout parameters whose values are needed within the calling component and for cases where the called procedure may raise exceptions which need to be handled by the calling component.

requirements.original: The response and exception handling part of the call operation makes use of getreply and catch operations to provide the required functionality.
requirements.canonical: The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation uses `getreply` and `catch` operations.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.1 -- The response and exception handling part of the call operation makes use of getreply and catch operations to provide the required functionality.

requirements.original: a) specifies the port at which the operation shall take place;
requirements.canonical: The receive part of a receiving operation SHALL specify the port at which the operation takes place.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- a) specifies the port at which the operation shall take place;

requirements.original: b) defines an optional matching part which specifies the acceptable input which will match the statement;
requirements.canonical: The receive part of a receiving operation MAY contain a matching part that specifies the acceptable input matching the operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- b) defines an optional matching part which specifies the acceptable input which will match the statement;

requirements.original: c) gives an optional address expression that uniquely identifies the communication partner (in case of one-to-many connections).
requirements.canonical: The receive part of a receiving operation MAY contain an address expression that uniquely identifies the communication partner in one-to-many connections.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- c) gives an optional address expression that uniquely identifies the communication partner (in case of one-to-many connections).

requirements.original: The port name and operation name shall be present.
requirements.canonical: A receiving operation SHALL contain the port name and the operation name.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- The port name and operation name shall be present.

requirements.original: The matching part needs only be present if the content of the received communication shall be restricted.
requirements.canonical: The matching part of a receiving operation NEED NOT be present unless the content of the received communication is to be restricted.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- The matching part needs only be present if the content of the received communication shall be restricted.

requirements.original: The identification of the communication partner (denoted by the from keyword) is optional and need only be specified in cases of one-to-many connections where the receiving entity needs to be explicitly identified.
requirements.canonical: The identification of the communication partner (`from` clause) in a receiving operation NEED NOT be specified except in one-to-many connections where the communication partner needs to be explicitly identified.

ambiguity.issue: The text says "receiving entity" although the entity identified by the from clause is the sending communication partner.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- The identification of the communication partner (denoted by the from keyword) is optional and need only be specified in cases of one-to-many connections where the receiving entity needs to be explicitly identified.

requirements.original: The assignment part in a receiving operation is optional.
requirements.canonical: The assignment part of a receiving operation MAY be omitted.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- The assignment part in a receiving operation is optional.

requirements.original: For message-based ports it is used when it is required to store received messages.
requirements.canonical: For message-based ports, the assignment part of a receiving operation stores the received message.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- For message-based ports it is used when it is required to store received messages.

requirements.original: In the case of procedure-based ports it is used for storing the in and inout parameters of an accepted call, for storing the return value or for storing exceptions.
requirements.canonical: For procedure-based ports, the assignment part of a receiving operation stores the `in` and `inout` parameters of an accepted call, the return value or the exception.

ambiguity.issue: Only getcall stores in/inout parameters; getreply stores out/inout parameters, which the sentence does not mention. Chosen reading: the text lists examples per operation kind.
readings: The assignment part of a getcall operation stores in and inout parameters, that of a getreply operation the return value (and out/inout parameters), and that of a catch operation the exception.
The assignment part of any procedure-based receiving operation stores only in and inout parameters, return values or exceptions.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- In the case of procedure-based ports it is used for storing the in and inout parameters of an accepted call, for storing the return value or for storing exceptions.

requirements.original: For the message or parameter value assignment part strong typing is not required, e.g. the variable used for storing a message shall be type-compatible to the type of the incoming message.
requirements.canonical: Strong typing IS NOT required for the message or parameter value assignment part of a receiving operation.

ambiguity.issue: "strong typing is not required" followed by "e.g. ... shall be type-compatible" is contradictory in wording; chosen reading: type compatibility instead of type identity is sufficient.
readings: The variable in a value or parameter assignment SHALL be type-compatible with, but need not be of the same type as, the received value.
No type check is performed for value or parameter assignments of a receiving operation.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- For the message or parameter value assignment part strong typing is not required, e.g. the variable used for storing a message shall be type-compatible to the type of the incoming message.

requirements.original: For the message or parameter value assignment part strong typing is not required, e.g. the variable used for storing a message shall be type-compatible to the type of the incoming message.
requirements.canonical: The variable used for storing a received message SHALL be type-compatible with the type of the incoming message.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- For the message or parameter value assignment part strong typing is not required, e.g. the variable used for storing a message shall be type-compatible to the type of the incoming message.

requirements.original: In addition, the assignment part may also be used to assign the sender address of a message, exception, reply or call to a variable.
requirements.canonical: The assignment part of a receiving operation MAY assign the sender address of a message, exception, reply or call to a variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- In addition, the assignment part may also be used to assign the sender address of a message, exception, reply or call to a variable.

requirements.original: For receiving operations using the any port from a port array construction (see clause 22.2.2), the assignment part may also be used to store the indices that identify the specific port instance where the receiving operation matched.
requirements.canonical: For a receiving operation using `any from` on a port array, the assignment part MAY store the indices that identify the port instance where the receiving operation matched.
requirements.condition: the receiving operation uses any from a port array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- For receiving operations using the any port from a port array construction (see clause 22.2.2), the assignment part may also be used to store the indices that identify the specific port instance where the receiving operation matched.

requirements.original: If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the @nodefault modifier can be placed before it to indicate that the implicit alt statement containing the operation as an alternative shall have the @nodefault modifier.
requirements.canonical: If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the `@nodefault` modifier MAY be placed before it.
requirements.condition: the receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the @nodefault modifier can be placed before it to indicate that the implicit alt statement containing the operation as an alternative shall have the @nodefault modifier.

requirements.original: If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the @nodefault modifier can be placed before it to indicate that the implicit alt statement containing the operation as an alternative shall have the @nodefault modifier.
requirements.canonical: If a `@nodefault` modifier is placed before a stand-alone receiving operation, the implicit `alt` statement containing the operation as an alternative SHALL have the `@nodefault` modifier.
requirements.condition: a @nodefault modifier precedes a stand-alone receiving operation
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.1.4.2 -- If a receiving operation is used as a stand-alone statement, the @nodefault modifier can be placed before it to indicate that the implicit alt statement containing the operation as an alternative shall have the @nodefault modifier.
